text:
Account types > Checking accounts
A Tidewell Bank checking account is for everyday spending, bill payments, and deposits. Checking accounts come with a debit card and have a monthly account fee of $16.95.

Account types > Savings accounts
A Tidewell Bank savings account is for setting money aside and earning interest. Savings accounts don't come with a debit card.

Account types > Tax-Free Savings Accounts (TFSA)
A Tidewell Bank TFSA lets eligible customers save while earning tax-free growth, within the annual contribution limits set by the government. For questions about TFSA contribution limits, call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199.

Account types > Viewing your accounts in chat
After verifying your identity in chat, you can see all of your Tidewell Bank accounts and their current balances.

Account types > Opening or closing an account
Accounts can't be opened or closed through chat. To open or close an account, call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199, Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm.

Contacting support and escalations > Contacting Tidewell Bank support
Tidewell Bank support can be reached at 1-800-555-0199, Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm.

section: Speaking with a specialist from chat
text:
Contacting support and escalations > Speaking with a specialist from chat
If you'd like to speak with a person, you can ask at any time in chat. We'll create a support ticket with a summary of your conversation, so you won't need to explain everything again. You'll receive a reference number starting with ESC.

section: When a specialist will contact you
text:
Contacting support and escalations > When a specialist will contact you
For verified customers, a specialist calls the phone number on file. Suspected fraud is urgent, and a specialist calls within 1 hour. High-priority issues receive a call within 4 business hours, and all other requests within 1 business day.

section: If your identity couldn't be verified
text:
Contacting support and escalations > If your identity couldn't be verified
If your identity couldn't be verified in chat, we can still create a support ticket, but we can't call you back. Call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199 and quote your reference number.

Contacting support and escalations > What chat can help with
After verifying your identity in chat, you can view your accounts and recent transactions, freeze a card, dispute a charge, and request a courtesy fee reversal. For anything else, a specialist can help.

section: When you can dispute a charge
text:
Disputing a transaction > When you can dispute a charge
You can dispute a posted charge on your Tidewell Bank account if you didn't make it, didn't receive what you paid for, were charged twice, or were charged the wrong amount. Disputes must be filed within 60 days of the transaction date.

Disputing a transaction > Pending charges
Pending charges can't be disputed until they post, which usually takes a few business days. Many charges that look wrong while pending, such as hotel or gas station holds, are corrected automatically when they post.

section: What happens after you file a dispute
text:
Disputing a transaction > What happens after you file a dispute
When you file a dispute, you receive a case number starting with DSP. A specialist reviews every dispute and contacts you within 10 business days. Each charge can only be disputed once; if a dispute already exists for a charge, we'll share its case number and status.

Disputing a transaction > Unauthorized charges
If you dispute a charge because you didn't make it, Tidewell Bank also recommends freezing the card used for the charge, so no further unauthorized purchases can be made.

Disputing a transaction > Fees can't be disputed
Fees, such as overdraft or NSF fees, can't be disputed. Eligible overdraft and NSF fees can be refunded through a courtesy reversal instead. See "Fees and courtesy reversals."

Disputing a transaction > Charges older than 60 days
Charges older than 60 days can't be disputed through chat. To ask about an older charge, call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199, Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm.

Disputing a transaction > Deposits and incoming payments
Deposits, transfers into your account, and other incoming payments can't be disputed, because no money left your account.

Fees and courtesy reversals > Fee schedule
Tidewell Bank charges the following fees: an overdraft fee of $45.00, an NSF (non-sufficient funds) fee of $48.00, a wire transfer fee of $25.00, and a monthly account fee of $16.95 on checking accounts.

Fees and courtesy reversals > Courtesy reversals
As a courtesy, Tidewell Bank can reverse one overdraft or NSF fee every 12 months (365 days). To be eligible, the fee must have been charged within the last 90 days. You can request a courtesy reversal in chat after verifying your identity.

section: Fees that aren't eligible for a courtesy reversal
text:
Fees and courtesy reversals > Fees that aren't eligible for a courtesy reversal
Wire transfer fees and monthly account fees aren't eligible for courtesy reversals. Overdraft and NSF fees charged more than 90 days ago also aren't eligible.

section: If you've already had a courtesy reversal
text:
Fees and courtesy reversals > If you've already had a courtesy reversal
Only one courtesy reversal is available every 12 months. If you've had a courtesy reversal in the last 12 months, you become eligible again 12 months after the date of that reversal.

section: What happens when a fee is reversed
text:
Fees and courtesy reversals > What happens when a fee is reversed
A reversed fee is credited back immediately to the account it was charged to. You receive a reference number starting with FR, and the refund appears in your transactions as a separate credit, such as "Overdraft Fee Reversal." The original fee also stays in your transaction history.

section: If you think a fee was charged in error
text:
Fees and courtesy reversals > If you think a fee was charged in error
If you believe a fee was charged by mistake and it isn't eligible for a courtesy reversal, call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199, Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm.

section: What Tidewell Bank will never ask for
text:
Fraud and scams > What Tidewell Bank will never ask for
Tidewell Bank will never ask for your full card number, PIN, online banking password, or a one-time passcode, whether by phone, email, text, or chat. In chat, we only ask for your full name, date of birth, and the last 4 digits of your card to verify your identity.

Fraud and scams > Signs of a scam
Be cautious of messages that create urgency, ask you to move money to "protect" it, ask for passcodes, or claim to be from Tidewell Bank but come from an unfamiliar number or address. When in doubt, contact Tidewell Bank directly at 1-800-555-0199.

section: If you suspect fraud on your account
text:
Fraud and scams > If you suspect fraud on your account
If you see charges you don't recognize, freeze your card right away, then dispute any unauthorized charges within 60 days of the transaction date. If you've found several unauthorized charges, or charges older than 60 days, our fraud team can review your account. Suspected fraud is treated as urgent, and a fraud specialist calls verified customers within 1 hour.

section: If you shared information with a scammer
text:
Fraud and scams > If you shared information with a scammer
If you shared your card details, PIN, password, or a passcode with someone, freeze your card and call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199 immediately.

section: Freezing a lost or stolen card
text:
Lost or stolen cards > Freezing a lost or stolen card
If your Tidewell Bank card is lost, stolen, or has been used without your permission, you can freeze it in chat after verifying your identity. Freezing a card takes effect immediately, and new purchases on the card are declined.

Lost or stolen cards > What freezing a card does
A frozen card can't be used for new purchases. Your accounts stay open, and the money in them is not affected. Freezing a card does not cancel or replace it.

Lost or stolen cards > Unfreezing or replacing a card
Cards can't be unfrozen or replaced through chat. To unfreeze a card or order a replacement card, call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199, Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm.

Lost or stolen cards > Cancelled cards
A cancelled card can no longer be used, so it can't be frozen. If a cancelled card is lost or stolen, no further action is needed for that card.

section: If someone used your card without permission
text:
Lost or stolen cards > If someone used your card without permission
If someone used your card without permission, freeze the card first to stop any new charges. Then review your recent transactions and dispute any charges you didn't make. For more details, see "Disputing a transaction" and "Fraud and scams."

Overdraft and NSF fees explained > What an overdraft fee is
An overdraft fee of $45.00 is charged when Tidewell Bank approves a payment even though your account doesn't have enough money to cover it, leaving your balance below zero.

Overdraft and NSF fees explained > What an NSF fee is
An NSF (non-sufficient funds) fee of $48.00 is charged when a payment is declined or returned because your account doesn't have enough money to cover it.

section: How to avoid overdraft and NSF fees
text:
Overdraft and NSF fees explained > How to avoid overdraft and NSF fees
To avoid overdraft and NSF fees, check your balance before large purchases, and remember that pending transactions will reduce your balance when they post. Keeping a small buffer in your checking account helps cover unexpected charges.

section: Getting an overdraft or NSF fee refunded
text:
Overdraft and NSF fees explained > Getting an overdraft or NSF fee refunded
Eligible overdraft and NSF fees can be refunded through a courtesy reversal, available once every 12 months for fees charged within the last 90 days. See "Fees and courtesy reversals."

Pending and posted transactions > What a pending transaction is
A pending transaction is a purchase or payment that has been authorized but not yet finalized. The amount is held from your available balance until the transaction posts.

Pending and posted transactions > When pending transactions post
Most pending transactions post within a few business days. The final amount can differ from the pending amount, for example with hotel, gas station, or restaurant charges that include holds or tips.

Pending and posted transactions > Disputing a pending transaction
Pending transactions can't be disputed until they post. If a charge still looks wrong after it posts, you can dispute it within 60 days of the transaction date.

Pending and posted transactions > Viewing your transactions in chat
After verifying your identity in chat, you can see your transactions from the last 30 days, or from up to the last 90 days. Each transaction shows whether it's pending or posted.

section: How we protect your account in chat
text:
Privacy and security > How we protect your account in chat
Tidewell Bank verifies your identity before sharing or changing any account information. We only share information about your own accounts, and never about another customer's accounts, even if you know their details.

Privacy and security > Information we'll never ask for
Tidewell Bank will never ask for your full card number, PIN, online banking password, or one-time passcodes, in chat or anywhere else.

Privacy and security > Keeping your information safe
Don't share your card details, PIN, or passwords with anyone, including people who say they work for Tidewell Bank. Use a strong, unique password for online banking.

section: If you think your account was accessed without permission
text:
Privacy and security > If you think your account was accessed without permission
If you think someone accessed your account without permission, freeze your card in chat and call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199 right away. See "Fraud and scams" for more steps.

Transfers and limits > Transfers between your own accounts
You can move money between your own Tidewell Bank accounts in online banking at no cost. Transfers between your own accounts are usually immediate.

Transfers and limits > Wire transfers
Wire transfers send money to other banks, including banks in other countries. Each wire transfer has a fee of $25.00, and wire transfer fees aren't eligible for courtesy reversals.

Transfers and limits > Transfer limits
You can send up to $3,000 per day to other people, and up to $10,000 per day by wire transfer. To ask about a higher limit, call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199.

Transfers and limits > Transfers in chat
Transfers can't be made through chat. To move or send money, use online banking or call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199, Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm.

Verifying your identity > Why we verify your identity
Before sharing or changing any account information, Tidewell Bank confirms that you are the account holder. This protects your money and personal information from anyone trying to access your account.

section: What we ask for in chat
text:
Verifying your identity > What we ask for in chat
To verify your identity in chat, Tidewell Bank asks for your full name, your date of birth, and the last 4 digits of your Tidewell Bank card. We never ask for your full card number, PIN, online banking password, or one-time passcodes.

Verifying your identity > If verification doesn't work
If the details you provide don't match our records, you can try again. For your security, identity verification in chat is locked after three unsuccessful attempts. If this happens, call Tidewell Bank support at 1-800-555-0199, Monday to Friday, 8am to 8pm.

section: Questions you can ask without verifying
text:
Verifying your identity > Questions you can ask without verifying
You can ask general questions about Tidewell Bank's policies, fees, and services without verifying your identity. Verification is only required to view or change information about your own accounts.
